answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, whose escape probability is controlled by conductance. A Sybil cluster can gain influence only through its sparse external cut: low conductance limits stationary flow into the cluster, while min-cut transitivity bounds prevent many identities from amplifying one weak inlet. Consequently, aggregate voting weight is capped by the cut, with delta measuring leakage rather than allowing an unbounded trust plume.
